findings.evidence: `run_claimed_post_merge` re-raises `PostMergeEnvironmentError`. The generic `except Exception` in `lifecycle_workers.py` (~1465-1476) then calls `release_claim`, which posts a `released` result. `is_claimable` (~331-334) requires `release_count < MAX_RELEASES` (= 3). The escalation is skipped for post-merge kinds (`job["kind"] not in POST_MERGE_KINDS`). So three rounds hitting `process-check-unavailable` leave the cleanup job id unclaimable. `post_merge_progress` still derives that attempt as the next job, so there is no `post_merge_exhausted` and no attention, and `reoffer-post-merge` refuses it with 'no exhausted post-merge obligation'. This contradicts the new spec scenario 'the next derivation offers the same attempt again'. The `lsof` PATH precheck makes this unlikely, but a cleanup-time `process-check-unavailable` that gets past the precheck would still get here. No test covers repeated releases.
findings.summary: An environment failure spends no attempt, but its released claim still counts against the job's release limit. After 3 such releases the job can no longer be claimed, and nothing reports it.
